text:
Marathon Petroleum recovered 2.8% today after hitting a three-week low yesterday, following a sharp 7% sell-off over the past two weeks. The bounce reflects stabilization around reduced oil prices (US crude at $103/barrel versus the $123/barrel global benchmark) and a critical leadership change announced on October 29th with an accompanying company update—details on strategy or operational changes that appear to have reset investor sentiment after the recent decline. Refineries are running at 92.8% capacity with moderate fuel inventories, supporting the company's operational backdrop.

The broader context matters here: while oil earnings have surged across Big Oil due to tight fuel supplies and refining margins, investor caution emerged this week around earnings guidance and a political contradiction—Trump's campaign promises of sub-$2 gasoline have not materialized, and his public criticism of Big Oil profits may signal potential policy headwinds, even as the refining sector remains genuinely profitable. The leadership transition at Marathon may therefore signal internal repositioning ahead of a period of scrutiny.
